Krichene and Rendle’s [On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; fixing 99 negatives ensures reproducibility but does not establish full-catalog superiority. [A Revisiting Study of Appropriate Offline Evaluation](https://doi.org/10.1145/3545796) empirically documents ranking differences between sampled and full-ranking evaluation. Candidate-sampling bias and repeated-selection bias are separate problems.

For this benchmark, retain each variant’s binary hit outcome for every identical user/candidate set. Recommended analysis: compute paired differences and a 95% stratified paired-bootstrap interval, resampling users within each category while preserving model pairs; recompute the equally weighted four-category macro difference each replicate. Report category differences and discordant win/loss counts; exact McNemar tests suit category-level binary outcomes, while paired randomization can assess the macro difference. These recommendations draw on [Dietterich](https://doi.org/10.1162/089976698300017197) and [Smucker et al.](https://maroo.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=744). Each additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Users—not 99 negatives or checkpoints—are the sampling units.

Predeclare checkpoint frequency, stopping rule, trial budget, macro-HR selection rule, and deterministic tie-breaking; apply comparable selection opportunities across variants. Keep preprocessing/training seeds 0/42, log every attempted configuration and inspected checkpoint, and freeze the final predictor before independent held-out evaluation. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) documents overfitting of selection criteria. After adaptive validation search, ordinary intervals/p-values remain exploratory: they omit selection optimism, training-seed variability, and candidate-resampling uncertainty. Four categories cannot establish cross-domain generalization; unseen items are not verified negatives, and neither sampled validation nor twenty-user recommendation diagnostics establishes full-catalog or online quality.
